Hi Kate —

Great questions, and thanks for the pipeline export — that helps a lot. High-level proposals below; happy to sync if you prefer a quick call.

- Intro validation: default is "first-touch" lock with a 7-day validation window. Meaning: the partner who first registers/intros the lead gets a 7-calendar-day period to submit required validation evidence (contact, intro email, MA POC). If the first-touch partner fails to validate within 7 days, the record reopens for other partners to claim.

- Intro-lock duration: once a validated intro converts to a paying account, we lock attribution to that partner for 90 days (intro-lock) unless a co-sell exception is approved (see below).

- Proration & payout computation: commissions are paid on recognized monthly recurring revenue (MRR). For mid-month activations we prorate the first payout to the percentage of active days in the billing month. For upgrades/downgrades, payouts adjust on the month of billing change (no retroactive adjustments beyond 60 days).

- Co-sell / dual-work exception: if a second partner performs >25% of definable technical work (e.g., build, deployment, customer-success-managed onboarding) within 30 days of contract signature, we evaluate a split (typical baseline 60/40 to first-touch but negotiable). Must be approved by Partner Ops and Sales.

I pulled together a couple of concrete examples and will cc Marissa (partner compensation) who has a CSV with proration scenarios. If this looks OK, we'll produce a short MOU and the intro-validation checklist you can attach to your deal record.

Next steps: do you want a 20-min slot tomorrow or shall we send a terse policy doc?

Hi Kate —

Looping in finance/ops context. A couple of operational clarifications and a sample CSV attached (pro-rating-examples.csv):

- Example A: Customer signs on 11/21, first invoice cycles on 12/01 for a full month. If partner introduced on 11/05 (validated), partner receives full month commission on 12/01 payout.

- Example B: Customer signs on 11/18 and is billed 11/18–12/18 pro rata; partner payout for the initial invoice is prorated to active days (we show the math in the CSV).

- Upsells: If the customer upgrades in month 2, the incremental MRR from the upgrade is credited in the month the upgrade is billed. We don't claw back prior commissions unless the customer cancels within Redwood's standard refund window (30 days).

- Co-sell splits: for co-sell cases where both partners bring demonstrable technical work, our standard approval splits are 60/40 (first-touch gets 60%). To move to a 50/50 split we require documented evidence of parity (joint SOW or signed statement of work).

Hi Kate —

Thanks for the clear asks. Below is the proposed partner policy text we can sign off on (short form) — this covers the adjustable validation windows, tiered intro-lock, proration rules, and exception paths. If this looks good I will route the MOU + DocuSign link and the intro-validation-form (attached) for BlueSky to sign.

1) Intro validation window (configurable): default = 7 days. On request from a named strategic partner, Redwood may set validation window to 14 or 30 days; this must be requested in writing at account registration and approved by Partner Ops.

2) Intro-lock tiers: Standard = 90 days post-conversion. Mid-market (> $50k ARR) = 180 days; Enterprise (> $250k ARR) = 365 days. Exceptions for co-sell may be approved by Partner Ops + Sales.

3) Attribution: First validated intro wins. Validation requires either (a) partner-submitted intro email thread showing clear handoff, (b) completed intro-validation-form (attached), or (c) mutual action plan signed by the customer and partner within the validation window. If the first partner fails validation within the window the opportunity reopens.

4) Proration & payouts: Commissions paid on recognized MRR. First invoice prorated to days active in billing cycle. Upsell incremental MRR credited the month it's billed. No retroactive adjustments beyond 60 days except for refunds/cancellations within Redwood's 30-day policy.

5) Co-sell exceptions: If a second partner contributes >25% measurable technical effort within 30 days of signature, submit joint evidence (SOW, deployment notes) within 10 days of invoice for a split review. Baseline split 60/40 to first-touch; 50/50 only with documented parity.

6) Operational mechanics: Submit claims via HubSpot partner record (link: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/BS-17) along with supporting materials. Partner Ops will review within 7 business days for standard cases; prioritized partner requests (validation window extension, tiered intro-lock) require a signed MOU and may take up to 10 business days.

Attachments included: intro-validation-form.xlsx, pro-rating-examples.csv (operational examples).
